- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for low sentiment periods.
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome > 3x recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or apply exponential decay to prevent runaway growth.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term (30d) trends in high volatility periods; add 15–25% buffer to forecast if sentiment shows rising momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67…), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment cycle midpoint.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 5x recent 7d average, model often fails to capture tail risk; apply a “volatility correction” by multiplying forecast by 0.8–0.9 if sentiment is neutral or negative.
